temples.Alternate_Name: Tirumala Balaji Temple; Tirupati Temple; Seven Hills Temple; Srivari Temple
temples.Temple_Type: Ancient Hill Temple Complex / Divya Desam
temples.Address: S V Temple, Tirumala, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh
temples.Secondary_Deities: Vakuladevi, Yoga Narasimha, Varadaraja, Garuda, Ramanuja, Vishwaksena
temples.Temple_Description: Perched atop the sacred Venkatadri hill of the Seshachalam range, Sri Venkateswara Temple is one of the world's most revered pilgrimage destinations. The self-manifested (Swayambhu) deity stands majestically under the gilded Ananda Nilayam vimana.
temples.Why_Famous: Kaliyuga Varada Swamy, Golden Ananda Nilayam Vimana, GI-tagged Tirupati Laddu Prasadam, over 1000 documented historic stone and copper inscriptions.
temples.Religious_Significance: Revered as the Kali Yuga Vaikuntha where Lord Vishnu resides to bestow grace and liberation upon devotees.
temples.Historical_Significance: Epigraphs record royal endowments from Pallava Queen Samavai (966 CE), Rajendra Chola, Kulottunga I, and emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara (1513–1524 CE).
temples.Construction_Period: Pallava, Chola, Pandya, and Vijayanagara dynastic additions (9th-16th c. CE)
temples.Founder: Traditional: King Thondaiman; Historical epigraphs: Consecrated since Sangam era
temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Thomala, Archana, Koluvu, Naivedyam, Sahasra Deepalankarana, Ekantha Seva
temples.Special_Pooja: Friday Abhishekam, Kalyanotsavam, Vasantotsavam, Sahasra Kalasabhishekam
temples.Ticket_Required: Optional (Free Sarva Darshan available; Paid SED ₹300)

temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available (Slotted Sarva Darshan SSD tokens at Alipiri, Tirupati Station, Srinivasam)

temples.Festival_Importance: Garuda Vahanam witnesses over 500,000 devotees circumambulating the Four Mada Streets.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Multi-tier parking at Alipiri and Ring Road, Tirumala)
temples.Elderly_Friendly: Yes (Supatham dedicated privileged entrance quota for 65+ and infant parents)

temples.Address: Tiruchanur Road, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh
temples.Secondary_Deities: Sri Krishna, Balarama, Sundararaja Swamy, Surya Narayana Swamy
temples.Temple_Description: The holy abode of Goddess Padmavathi, consort of Lord Venkateswara, seated on a golden lotus. Pilgrimage tradition holds that visiting Tirumala is fulfilled only after worshipping Devi Padmavathi at Tiruchanur.
temples.Why_Famous: Padma Sarovaram sacred tank, Karthika Brahmotsavam Panchami Theertham, golden rathotsavam.
temples.Religious_Significance: Incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi manifesting on a golden thousand-petaled lotus in Padma Sarovaram tank.
temples.Historical_Significance: Patronized by Chola, Pallava, and Vijayanagara monarchs with extensive stone inscriptions.

temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Sahasranamarchana, Kalyanotsavam, Unjal Seva, Ekantha Seva
temples.Major_Festivals: Karthika Brahmotsavam, Panchami Theertham, Vasantotsavam, Navaratri
temples.Festival_Importance: Lakhs take holy dip in Padma Sarovaram as the divine Chakra Theertham is bathed.
temples.Accommodation: Yes (TTD Choultries at Tiruchanur and Tirupati)

temples.Temple_Type: Pancha Bhoota Sthalam (Vayu Lingam) / Paadal Petra Sthalam
temples.Address: Srikalahasti, Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.Secondary_Deities: Goddess Gnana Prasunambika, Pathala Vinayaka, Kannappa
temples.Temple_Description: One of the five sacred Pancha Bhoota Sthalas representing the element Air (Vayu). The flame inside the sanctum flickers continuously even though there are no air vents. Famous worldwide for Rahu-Ketu Sarpa Dosha Nivarana pujas.
temples.Why_Famous: Vayu Lingam (Air element), Rahu-Ketu Sarpadosha Nivarana Puja, Pathala Vinayaka cave shrine, legend of Kannappa Nayanar.
temples.Religious_Significance: Representing Vayu in Pancha Bhoota Stalas; celebrated in Thevaram hymns by Sambandar and Appar.
temples.Historical_Significance: Constructed during 5th century CE by Pallavas; monumental gopurams added by Kulottunga Chola I and Krishnadevaraya in 1516 CE.
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Rahu Ketu Puja Batches: 06:30 AM to 06:00 PM continuously
temples.Daily_Pooja: Gomatha Pooja, Ushakala Abhishekam, Ucha Kala Pooja, Pradosha Pooja
temples.Special_Pooja: Rahu Ketu Sarpa Dosha Nivarana Puja (₹500, ₹1500, ₹2500, ₹5000)
temples.Ticket_Required: Optional (Free Darshan queue; Paid Puja tickets)
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available at Devasthanam counters outside and inside four gopurams
temples.Major_Festivals: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (13 days), Giri Pradakshina, Nandi Seva
temples.Festival_Importance: Over 300,000 pilgrims participate in the Rathotsavam and midnight Lingodbhava Abhishekam.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Swarnamukhi river bed and bypass parking)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Nitya Annadana scheme for all pilgrims)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Devasthanam guest houses: Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati choultries)
temples.Nearby_Temples: Tirupati Balaji (38 km), Gudimallam Parashurameswara (25 km)
temples.Nearby_Restaurants: Kalahasti Arya Bhavan, Hotel MGM Grand, Annapurna Veg
temples.Nearby_Historical_Places: Gudimallam ancient Shiva temple (2nd c. BCE), Chandragiri Fort
temples.Nearby_Nature_Attractions: Ubbalamadugu Falls (Tada Falls 35 km), Pulicat Lake (45 km)

temples.Alternate_Name: Srisailam Temple; Srisailam Jyotirlinga & Shakti Peetham
temples.Address: Srisailam, Nandyal District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.Secondary_Deities: Vriddha Mallikarjuna, Sahasra Linga, Vighneswara, Annapurna
temples.Temple_Description: One of India's rarest sacred sites that is simultaneously a Jyotirlinga of Lord Shiva and a Maha Shakti Peetham of Goddess Parvati (Bhramaramba). Surrounded by the pristine Nallamala forests overlooking the Pathalaganga (Krishna River).
temples.Why_Famous: 2nd Jyotirlinga, Bhramaramba Maha Shakti Peetham, Sparsha Darshan (touching Lingam), massive fortified enclosure with stone sculptures.
temples.Religious_Significance: Adi Shankaracharya composed the immortal Sivananda Lahari here; Akka Mahadevi attained union with Mallikarjuna in Kadalivana caves.
temples.Historical_Significance: Inscriptions from Satavahana, Ikshvaku, Kakatiya (Prataparudra), Reddi kings of Kondaveedu, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj who built the northern gopuram in 1677 CE.
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Garbhagriha Sparsha Darshan: 06:30 AM – 01:00 PM & 06:00 PM – 09:00 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Maha Mangala Harathi, Rudrabhishekam, Chandi Homam, Ekantha Seva
temples.Ticket_Required: Optional (Free Darshan available; ₹150 Special Entry; ₹500 Sparsha Darshan)
temples.Advance_Booking_Required: Recommended for Sparsha Darshan; Spot queues available
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available at CRO counters in Srisailam
temples.Major_Festivals: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (7 days), Ugadi Mahotsavam, Kumbhothsavam
temples.Festival_Importance: Paganalankarana (royal silk turban wrapping around the Vimana) witnessed by over 400,000 pilgrims.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Extensive vehicle parking at Srisailam entrance & Sunnipenta)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Nitya Annaprasada Bhavan serving thousands daily)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Ganga Sadan, Gauri Sadan, Mallikarjuna Sadan)

temples.Nearby_Hotels: APTDC Haritha Srisailam, Srisailam Forest Cottages
temples.Nearby_Historical_Places: Shivaji Spoorthy Kendram, Akka Mahadevi Caves (boat ride)

temples.Temple_Name: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam
temples.Temple_Name_Local: శ్రీ దుర్గా మల్లేశ్వర స్వామి వార్ల దేవస్థానం (కనకదుర్గ గుడి)
temples.Address: Indrakeeladri, Vijayawada, NTR District, Andhra Pradesh
temples.Secondary_Deities: Lord Malleswara Swamy, Subrahmanya Swamy, Nataraja
temples.Temple_Description: Standing majestically atop Indrakeeladri hill on the banks of the Krishna River in Vijayawada. Goddess Kanaka Durga is self-manifested (Swayambhu) with eight arms bearing divine weapons, holding the demon Mahishasura in battle victory.
temples.Why_Famous: Navaratri celebrations with different Alankarams daily, Teppotsavam (boat festival) on Krishna River, Indrakeeladri Ghat road panoramic views.
temples.Religious_Significance: Mentioned in Kalika Purana and Mahabharata as the sacred spot where Arjuna performed penance to obtain the Pasupatastra from Lord Shiva.
temples.Historical_Significance: Epigraphs of Western Chalukyas, Kakatiyas, and Reddy rulers document historic endowments.
temples.Founder: Traditional: Sage Indrakeela; Historical patronage: Chalukyas & Gajapatis
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Maha Harathi: 04:00 AM; Antaralaya Darshan ₹300: 06:00 AM – 08:00 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Snapana, Archana, Chandi Homam, Maha Naivedyam, Punnami Harathi
temples.Advance_Booking_Required: No; Spot queues available; Navaratri online recommended
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available at Hill Top and Foot Hill counters
temples.Major_Festivals: Dasara Navaratri (10 days), Shakambhari Utsavams, Bhavani Deeksha Viramana
temples.Festival_Importance: Over 1.5 million devotees gather during Dasara; grand Hamsa Vahana Teppotsavam on Krishna river.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Bhavani Ghat and Punnami Ghat parking with free temple shuttle buses)
temples.Elderly_Friendly: Yes (Ghat road lift and battery buggy cars from foothill)
temples.Prasadam_Available: Yes (Famous Kanaka Durga Pulihora, Laddu, Sakkara Pongali)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Sri Kanaka Durga Nitya Annadanam serves over 10,000 pilgrims daily)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Devasthanam cottages at Hilltop and Sitara Bhavan)

temples.Temple_Name_Local: శ్రీ లక్ష్మీ నరసింహ స్వామి దేవస్థానం యాదాద్రి
temples.Temple_Type: Ancient Cave Shrine & Modern Monolithic Krishna Shila Temple Complex
temples.Address: Yadagirigutta, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Narasimha (Pancha Narasimha Kshetram: Jwala, Yogananda, Gandabherunda, Ugra, Lakshmi Narasimha)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Goddess Lakshmi, Sri Rama, Anjaneya Swamy, Alwars
temples.Temple_Description: One of India's most breathtaking modern architectural reconstructions, rebuilt completely using 250,000 tonnes of pure black granite (Krishna Shila) based on Kakatiya and Dravidian temple treatises without concrete, encasing the ancient sanctum cave.
temples.Why_Famous: Complete Krishna Shila granite reconstruction, Pancha Narasimha forms in sanctum cave, golden Vimana, Ashtabuja prakaaram sculptures.
temples.Religious_Significance: Named after sage Yadarishi who performed penance; worshipped as a powerful healing deity for relief from spiritual and physical ailments.
temples.Historical_Significance: Mentioned in Skanda Purana; comprehensively rebuilt from 2016-2022 by the Telangana Government under master architect Anand Sai.
temples.Founder: Government of Telangana (YTDA) / Ancient sage Yadarishi
temples.Dynasty: Kakatiya traditions / Modern Telangana State Heritage Project
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: VIP Break Darshan: 09:00 AM – 10:00 AM & 04:00 PM – 05:00 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Nijabhishekam, Archana, Sudarshana Homam, Nitya Kalyanam, Pavalimpu Seva
temples.Ticket_Required: Optional (Free Dharma Darshan; ₹150 Special Entry; ₹300 VIP)
temples.Advance_Booking_Required: No; Spot ticketing available; Online booking option
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available at Hill Top Complex counters
temples.Major_Festivals: Annual Brahmotsavam (11 days), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathotsavam
temples.Festival_Importance: Tirukkalyanam and Divya Vimana Rathotsavam attended by over 300,000 devotees.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Massive 7,000-vehicle capacity parking at foothill with free electric buses)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Nitya Annadana Bhavan serves wholesome meals free to all visitors)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Yadadri Temple Development Authority Cottages and Choultries)

temples.Temple_Name_Local: శ్రీ సీతారామచంద్ర స్వామి వారి దేవస్థానం భద్రాచలం
temples.Address: Bhadrachalam, Bhadradri Kothagudem District, Telangana
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Rama (Vaikuntha Rama with conch, discus, bow, and arrow) & Sita Devi
temples.Secondary_Deities: Lakshmana, Bhadra Rishi, Anjaneya Swamy
temples.Temple_Description: Known as the Dakshina Ayodhya on the serene banks of sacred Godavari River. Lord Rama appears here uniquely in Vaikuntha Rama form with four arms holding Shankha, Chakra, Bow, and Arrow, with Sita Devi seated gracefully on his left lap.
temples.Why_Famous: Sri Rama Navami Kalyanam with pearls (Mutyala Talambralu) presented by Telangana Government, Kancharla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) historic compositions and prison jewels.
temples.Religious_Significance: Dandakaranya location where Lord Rama crossed the Godavari and blessed mountain Bhadra who performed penance.
temples.Historical_Significance: Constructed in 17th century by saint-composer Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna), Tahsildar of Palvancha under Tana Shah of Golconda Sultanate.
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Antaralaya Darshan: 06:30 AM – 11:30 AM & 06:00 PM – 08:30 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Suprabhatam, Abhishekam, Sahasranamarchana, Nitya Kalyanam, Rajabhogam, Pavalimpu Seva
temples.Special_Pooja: Nitya Kalyanam (Daily celestial wedding of Rama & Sita), Suvarna Pushparchana
temples.Major_Festivals: Sri Rama Navami (Kalyanotsavam), Vaikunta Ekadasi (Teppotsavam on Godavari)
temples.Festival_Importance: State festival attended by over 400,000 devotees; pearls sent on behalf of state governor.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Godavari river bed and Kalyana Mandapam grounds)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Nitya Annadana scheme for all pilgrims daily)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Bhakta Ramadasu Sadan, Soumitri Sadan, Sita Nilayam)

temples.Alternate_Name: Ramalingeswara Temple Palampet; UNESCO World Heritage Site
temples.Temple_Type: UNESCO World Heritage Site / Monumental Stone Temple
temples.Address: Palampet, Venkatapur Mandal, Mulugu District, Telangana
temples.Secondary_Deities: Nandi (Monolithic), Kameshwara, Kateshwara shrines
temples.Temple_Description: An inscription dates this Kakatiya marvel to 1213 CE, constructed under general Recharla Rudra. The only temple in India named after its master sculptor (Ramappa). Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 for its floating bricks technology, sandbox earthquake foundations, and bracket dancer statues.
temples.Why_Famous: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021), floating bricks in water (low density porous clay), earthquake-resistant sandbox technology, polished black dolerite bracket figures (Madanikas).
temples.Religious_Significance: Ancient Kakatiya Shaivite shrine with an imposing 9-foot Shivalingam in the star-shaped Garbhagriha.
temples.Historical_Significance: Stone inscription of 1213 CE recording King Ganapati Deva and Recharla Rudra; praised by Marco Polo as 'the brightest star in the galaxy of medieval temples'.
temples.Founder: Recharla Rudra (General of Kakatiya King Ganapati Deva); Chief Sculptor: Ramappa
temples.Daily_Pooja: Daily Archana, Rudrabhishekam conducted by resident archaka
temples.Special_Pooja: Maha Shivaratri Abhishekam, Kartika Masam Deepotsavam
temples.Ticket_Required: Yes (ASI entry ticket ₹25 for Indians, ₹300 foreigners; free for children under 15)
temples.Advance_Booking_Required: No; ASI QR code tickets at entry gate
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Available at ASI ticketing counter at entrance
temples.Major_Festivals: Maha Shivaratri (3-day fair), Ramappa Dance Festival (Kakatiya Heritage Festival)
temples.Festival_Importance: Classical dancers from across the world perform before the historic Madanika brackets.
temples.Wheelchair_Access: Yes (Ramps at outer perimeter; stone plinth stepped)
temples.Nearby_Temples: Thousand Pillar Temple (68 km), Bhadrakali Temple Warangal (66 km)
temples.Nearby_Restaurants: Haritha Restaurant Ramappa, Lake View Dhaba Palampet
temples.Nearby_Hotels: Haritha Lake View Resort Ramappa, Hotel Ashoka Warangal
temples.Nearby_Historical_Places: Warangal Fort (70 km), Ghanpur Group of Temples (Kota Gullu 10 km)
temples.Nearby_Nature_Attractions: Ramappa Lake (boating available 1 km), Laknavaram Lake (28 km)
temples.Nearby_Hospitals: Community Health Centre Venkatapur (10 km), Mulugu District Hospital (22 km)
temples.Nearby_Fuel_Stations: Indian Oil Petrol Bunk Venkatapur (9 km)
temples.Nearby_Transport: Kazipet Junction / Warangal Station (68 km), Hyderabad Airport (210 km)

temples.Historical_Significance: Inscriptions covering the base detailing donations of jewelry, lands, temple dancers, musicians, accountants, and bronze casters by Raja Raja Chola I.

Sthaneshwar Mahadev is the ancient temple where the Pandavas and Lord Krishna worshipped Lord Shiva and received his blessings for victory in the Mahabharata War.

temples.Religious_Significance: Bathing here during a Solar Eclipse confers the spiritual merit of performing thousands of Ashwamedha Yagnas; described by Abul Fazl as the 'miniature ocean'.
temples.Historical_Significance: Capital of King Harshavardhana (7th century CE); described in the memoirs of Chinese traveler Xuanzang.

temples.Religious_Significance: Abode of Bhagwan Swaminarayan embodying universal peace, Vedic Sanatana Dharma values, and selfless spiritual service.
temples.Historical_Significance: Inaugurated on November 6, 2005 by President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and Pramukh Swami Maharaj; carved by 7,000 artisans and 3,000 volunteers.

temples.Temple_Description: Located at an altitude of 5,200 feet in the fold of the three-peaked Trikuta Mountain. The Holy Cave houses no idols; devotees worship the sacred natural rock manifestations known as the Holy Pindies representing Maha Kali (destructive/protective force), Maha Lakshmi (wealth/prosperity), and Maha Saraswati (wisdom/learning), bathed continuously by icy natural spring waters.

temples.Religious_Significance: Goddess Vaishnavi performed severe austerities to unite with Lord Rama; granted immortality to dwell at Trikuta to protect devotees until Kali Yuga ends.
temples.Historical_Significance: Discovered by Pandit Shridhar in the medieval era; administered since 1986 by the statutory Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (SMVDSB) established by Governor Jagmohan.

temples.Construction_Period: Ancient Cave; modernized platforms and tracks 1986–Present

temples.Temple_Description: The holy samadhi shrine of the 19th-century saint Shree Sai Baba who taught 'Sabka Malik Ek' (One God Governs All) and 'Shraddha & Saburi' (Faith and Patience). temples.Historical_Significance: Sai Baba lived in Shirdi from approximately 1858 until his Mahasamadhi on Vijayadasami, October 15, 1918; stone structure built by disciple Gopalrao Buti.

temples.Alternate_Name: Trimbak Temple; Tenth Jyotirlinga; Source of Godavari

temples.Religious_Significance: Primary centre for Narayan Nagbali, Kalsarpa Shanti, and Tripindi Shraddha rituals in India; Sage Gautama performed penance here to bring Ganga down.
temples.Historical_Significance: Present monumental black basalt stone temple constructed by Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb) between 1755 and 1786 CE.

temples.Main_Deity: Shree Siddhivinayak (Two-and-a-half-foot monolithic black stone Ganesha with right-turning trunk - Navasacha Ganpati)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Riddhi and Siddhi (Goddesses of wealth and accomplishment on either side)
temples.Temple_Description: One of the richest and most frequently visited shrines in Mumbai. Consecrated in 1801 CE. The black stone deity features four arms holding a lotus, axe, modak, and prayer beads, flanked by Goddesses Riddhi and Siddhi. The gold-plated inner sanctum roof is adorned with 3.75 kg of pure gold.
temples.Why_Famous: Navasacha Ganpati (grantor of all wishes), right-turning trunk (Siddhi Vinayak), gold-plated sanctum dome, Tuesday massive pilgrim queues, celebrity and global dignitary visits.
temples.Religious_Significance: Right-turning trunk Ganesha is considered especially potent, demanding strict spiritual adherence and granting immense success and prosperity.
temples.Historical_Significance: Originally consecrated on November 19, 1801, funded by a wealthy childless agri woman Deubai Patil so other women would be blessed with children.
temples.Architectural_Style: Modern Multi-Angled Nagara & Pancharatna Style with Gold Spire

temples.Temple_Name_Local: શ્રી સોમનાથ જ્યોતિર્લિંગ મંદિર પ્રભાસ પાટણ
temples.Alternate_Name: First Jyotirlinga; Somnath Patan; Shrine Eternal
temples.Address: Somnath Mandir Road, Prabhas Patan, Gir Somnath, Gujarat
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Shiva (Somnath - Lord of Soma / Moon God)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Parvati Devi, Ganesha, Hanuman, Baan Stambh (Arrow Pillar)
temples.Temple_Description: The foremost of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, perched on the windswept Arabian Sea shore where rivers Hiran, Kapila, and mythical Saraswati meet. Celebrated as the 'Shrine Eternal', rebuilt seven times across millennia following historical invasions. Reconstructed in pristine Kailash Mahameru Prasad style under Iron Man Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
temples.Why_Famous: First of the 12 Jyotirlingas (Prathama Jyotirlinga), Baan Stambh (pillar with arrow pointing unimpeded to Antarctica), rebuilt by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Sound and Light show (Jay Somnath) with Amitabh Bachchan narration.
temples.Religious_Significance: Chandra (Moon God) was cured of his wasting curse by Lord Shiva after intense penance here; praised in Rigveda.
temples.Historical_Significance: Rebuilt by Sardar Patel following his Diwali 1947 pledge; consecrated by India's first President Dr. Rajendra Prasad on May 11, 1951.
temples.Architectural_Style: Maru-Gurjara (Chaulukya / Solanki Dynasty Revival by Sompura Sculptors)
temples.Construction_Period: Ancient origin; 7th stone reconstruction completed 1951 CE
temples.Founder: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Reconstruction) & Prabhas Sompura Artisans
temples.Dynasty: Chaulukya / Solanki / Modern Republic of India

temples.Special_Pooja: Dhwajarohan Seva (hoisting sacred flag atop 155-ft Shikhara), Someshwar Mahapuja, Rudrabhishek

temples.Festival_Importance: Continuous 42-hour temple opening on Shivaratri; over 500,000 pilgrims attend the coastal fair.

temples.Alternate_Name: Dwarka Temple; King of Dwarka; Mokshapuri Dwarka; Char Dham
temples.Temple_Type: Char Dham Pilgrimage Site / Sapta Puri / 108 Divya Desams
temples.Address: Dwarkadhish Temple, Dwarka, Devbhumi Dwarka District, Gujarat
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Krishna as Dwarkadhish (King of Dwarka in four-armed royal Trivikrama posture)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Balram, Subhadra, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Devaki, Satyabhama, Jambavati, Radhika
temples.Temple_Description: One of the four supreme Char Dham sites and one of the seven Mokshadayani Puris. The majestic 5-storey Jagat Mandir is supported by 72 limestone pillars, crowned by a 78-metre spire that flies a colossal 52-yard flag (Dhwaja) depicting the sun and moon, visible from 10 km at sea and changed five times daily.
temples.Why_Famous: Char Dham site, 52-yard sacred flag changed 5 times a day, Mokshada Mokshapuri, Gomti Ghat with 56 steps (Chhappan Padi), underwater ancient sunken city of Krishna discovered by Marine Archaeology.
temples.Religious_Significance: Capital city founded by Lord Krishna after leaving Mathura; pilgrimage brings liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
temples.Historical_Significance: Originally established by Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabha; present 16th-century temple incorporates 12th-century Chaulukya stone foundations; Adi Shankara established the Western Sharada Peetham here.
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Mangala Aarti: 07:00 AM; Shringar: 08:00 AM; Sandhya Aarti: 07:30 PM; Shayan Aarti: 08:30 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Mangala Aarti, Shringarbhog, Gwal Bhog, Rajbhog, Uthappan, Sandhya Aarti, Shayan Bhog
temples.Special_Pooja: Dhwaja Rohana Seva (52-gaj Dhwaja hoisting ceremony held five times daily)
temples.Offline_Ticket_Availability: Free entry via Moksha Dwar (entry gate) and Swarga Dwar (exit)
temples.Major_Festivals: Janmashtami Mahotsav, Holi (Dolyatra), Sharad Purnima, Annakut Utsav
temples.Festival_Importance: Midnight Kanha Janmotsav attended by over 500,000 devotees dancing with Garba and bhajans.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Organized parking at Gomti Ghat and Dwarka bypass)

temples.Accommodation: Yes (Toran Tourist Bungalow, Kokila Dhiraj Dham, Birla Dharamshala)

temples.Nearby_Restaurants: Chhappan Bhog Restaurant, Shrinath Dining Hall, Toran Dining Hall

temples.Alternate_Name: Pushkar Brahma Temple; Only Major Brahma Temple in India
temples.Temple_Type: Ancient Tirtharaj Shrine / Sole Prominent Brahma Temple
temples.Address: Brahma Temple Road, Pushkar, Ajmer District, Rajasthan
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Brahma (Chaturmukha four-faced life-size deity in Padmasana)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Goddess Gayatri, Savitri Devi (on Ratnagiri Hill above)
temples.Temple_Description: One of the very few surviving temples in the world dedicated to Lord Brahma, the Creator in the Hindu Trinity. Constructed with stone slabs and marble, topped with a distinctive red spire (Shikhara) and a goose (Hamsa) motif. The floor and inner walls are embedded with silver coins donated by devotees.
temples.Why_Famous: Only major temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the world, red shikhara with Hamsa bird, sacred Pushkar Lake bath, annual world-famous Pushkar Camel Fair (Kartik Mela).
temples.Religious_Significance: Pushkar is hailed as Tirtharaj (King of all pilgrimage centers); Lord Brahma dropped a lotus petal here to create the lake and performed a grand Vedic Yajna.
temples.Historical_Significance: Traditional origin dating to 14th century CE; consecrated by Sage Vishwamitra; renovated by Maharaja Jawat Raj of Marwar in 1809 CE.
temples.Founder: Traditional: Sage Vishwamitra; Historic: Maharaja Jawat Raj of Marwar
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Mangala Aarti: 05:30 AM; Sandhya Aarti: 07:00 PM; Ratri Shayan: 08:30 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Pratahkaal Aarti, Abhishek, Dhoop Deep, Sandhya Maha Aarti with Nagadas
temples.Special_Pooja: Kartik Purnima Mahapooja, Pushkar Sarovar Maha Aarti
temples.Major_Festivals: Pushkar Camel Fair & Kartik Purnima Maha Mela (International festival)
temples.Festival_Dates: Kartik Shukla Ekadasi to Kartik Purnima
temples.Festival_Importance: Attracts over 400,000 tourists and pilgrims worldwide; mass holy dip in Pushkar Lake.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Mela Ground Parking and Pushkar Marwar Bus Stand parking)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Charitable dharamshalas provide free meals to sadhus and pilgrims)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (RTDC Hotel Sarovar, Pushkar Resorts, Heritage Haveli Hotels)

temples.Temple_Name_Local: श्री महाकालेश्वर ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर उज्जैन मध्य प्रदेश
temples.Alternate_Name: Mahakal Ujjain; Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga; Mahakal Lok
temples.Temple_Type: Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga (3rd) / Sapta Puri / Kumbh Mela Tirtha
temples.Address: Mahakal Marg, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Shiva as Mahakaleshwar (The Lord of Time and Death - facing South / Dakshinavarti)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Omkareshwar (first floor), Nagchandreshwar (third floor, open only on Nag Panchami), Vriddha Mahakal
temples.Temple_Description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, revered as the sole Dakshinavarti (south-facing) Jyotirlinga, positioned at the prime meridian of ancient Indian astronomy. Renowned worldwide for the daily pre-dawn 'Bhasma Aarti' where the deity is worshipped with sacred cow-dung ash (vibhuti). The newly inaugurated 900-meter Mahakal Lok Corridor features 108 grand sculpted pillars depicting Lord Shiva's Anand Tandav.
temples.Why_Famous: Sole south-facing Jyotirlinga, pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti (04:00 AM), Nagchandreshwar temple (opened once a year on Nag Panchami), Mahakal Lok Corridor with 108 Shiv Stambhas and mural plazas.
temples.Religious_Significance: Ujjain is one of the seven Mokshadayani Sapta Puris; Mahakal is the celestial king and protector of the city.
temples.Historical_Significance: Mentioned in Kalidasa's Meghaduta; rebuilt by General Ranoji Shinde of the Maratha Scindia dynasty in 1734 CE; Mahakal Lok Corridor opened in 2022.
temples.Construction_Period: Ancient origin; present structure 1734 CE; Mahakal Lok 2022 CE
temples.Founder: Ranoji Shinde (Scindia Dynasty) / Government of Madhya Pradesh
temples.Dynasty: Avanti / Scindia of Gwalior / Modern MP Government

temples.Festival_Importance: Sehra Bandhan on Shivaratri morning; the deity wears a massive floral crown and Bhasma Aarti takes place at noon instead of dawn.

temples.Temple_Name_Local: माँ दंतेश्वरी शक्तिपीठ मंदिर दंतेवाड़ा छत्तीसगढ़
temples.Temple_Type: 51 Maha Shakti Peeth (Tooth of Sati) / Historic Royal Bastar Temple
temples.Locality: Confluence of Shankhini and Dankini Rivers
temples.Address: Dantewada, South Bastar, Chhattisgarh
temples.Main_Deity: Goddess Danteshwari (Six-armed black stone Mahishasuramardini holding sword, trident, discus, conch)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Bhairav, Ganesha, Garuda, Shankhini-Dankini river deities
temples.Temple_Description: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where the tooth (Daant) of Goddess Sati fell. Consecrated at the sacred holy confluence of Shankhini and Dankini rivers. Revered as the sovereign deity and Kuldevi of the royal family of Bastar and over 30 indigenous tribal communities who bring their local village deities (Angas and Chhatras) during Bastar Dussehra.
temples.Why_Famous: Tooth of Goddess Sati (Shakti Peeth), Bastar Dussehra (75-day festival - world's longest), unique amalgamation of tribal folk and Vedic rituals, Garuda pillar.
temples.Religious_Significance: Supreme spiritual guardian of the entire Dandakaranya forest region; sacred confluence of black Shankhini and white Dankini waters.
temples.Historical_Significance: Constructed in the 14th century CE by Maharaja Annama Deva, brother of Kakatiya King Prataparudra of Warangal, after migrating to Bastar in 1323 CE.
temples.Architectural_Style: Kakatiya & Indigenous Bastar Wooden-Roof Stone Architecture
temples.Founder: Maharaja Annama Deva (First King of Bastar Kakatiya Dynasty)
temples.Special_Darshan_Timings: Morning Mangal Aarti: 06:00 AM; Sandhya Aarti: 07:30 PM
temples.Daily_Pooja: Jalabhishek, Shodashopachara Puja, Chandi Path, Sandhya Maha Aarti with tribal horns and drums
temples.Special_Pooja: Navaratri Havan, Jyoti Kalash Sthapana (over 10,000 continuous oil lamps lit)
temples.Major_Festivals: Bastar Dussehra (75-day festival), Chaitra & Shardiya Navratri, Fagun Mela (10 days)
temples.Festival_Importance: Scores of tribal village shamans assemble carrying local deities on wooden litters to pay homage to Maa Danteshwari.
temples.Parking_Available: Yes (Temple trust ground near river bridge)
temples.Annadanam: Yes (Trust Bhojanalaya provides free afternoon meals)
temples.Accommodation: Yes (Danteshwari Temple Trust Guest House, PWD Rest House)

temples.Nearby_Restaurants: Annapurna Bhojanalaya Dantewada, Bastar Treat Restaurant
temples.Nearby_Hotels: Hotel Danteshwari Dantewada, CG Tourism Bafna Resort Jagdalpur

temples.Nearby_Nature_Attractions: Chitrakote Waterfalls (Niagara of India 95 km), Tirathgarh Waterfalls, Kanger Valley National Park
temples.Nearby_Transport: Dantewada Railway Station (KK Line 2 km), Jagdalpur Airport (85 km), Raipur Airport (370 km)

temples.Temple_Type: Historic Kuladevata Temple / Indo-Portuguese Goan Architectural Jewel
temples.Address: Priol, Ponda Taluka, North Goa, Goa
temples.Main_Deity: Lord Shiva as Manguesh (Incarnation born when Shiva playfully scared Parvati in tiger form)
temples.Secondary_Deities: Parvati Devi, Ganesha, Mulkeshwar, Virabhadra, Saanteri
temples.Temple_Description: One of the largest, most famous, and prominent Hindu temples in Goa. Famous for its magnificent seven-storey octagonal Deepastambha (lamp tower) which illuminates the entire courtyard when lit with hundreds of oil lamps. Features a distinctive blend of Goan Hindu, Maratha, and Indo-Portuguese architectural styles with pristine blue and white domes.
temples.Why_Famous: Seven-storey octagonal Deepastambha, distinctive Goan Indo-Portuguese dome architecture, water tank (Tali), legendary home of singing legends Lata Mangeshkar and Pt. Jitendra Abhisheki.
temples.Religious_Significance: Principal Kuladevata (family deity) of many Saraswat Brahmin families across India.
temples.Historical_Significance: Original temple was in Cortalim (Kushasthali); shifted secretly by night to Priol in 1560 CE to escape Portuguese Inquisition destruction; rebuilt by Marathas in 18th c. CE.
temples.Architectural_Style: Goan Temple Architecture (Unique blend of Hindu, Maratha, and Portuguese Baroquesque elements)

temples.Temple_Description: One of the four sacred Char Dham pilgrimage centers of India. Built inside the towering 20-foot Meghanada Pacheri stone walls. The 214-foot Rekha Deula sanctum houses the Holy Trinity carved out of sacred Margosa (neem) wood, crowned by the eight-metal Nilachakra and Patitapabana flag. Famous for the sacred Mahaprasad (Chhappan Bhog) cooked in earthen pots over woodfire.

temples.Historical_Significance: Present monumental temple initiated by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva in 1135 CE and completed by Anangabhima Deva III of Eastern Ganga Dynasty; visited by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu who lived 24 years here.

Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1984 as a pinnacle of Kalinga stone sculpture.

temples.Historical_Significance: Built around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty to commemorate his military victories; European sailors called it the 'Black Pagoda'.

temples.Religious_Significance: Bhavatarini means 'She who liberates her devotees from the ocean of worldly existence (Samsara)'; birthplace of the modern Ramakrishna-Vivekananda renaissance.
temples.Historical_Significance: Consecrated on Snana Yatra day, May 31, 1855 by Rani Rashmoni; Swami Vivekananda was introduced to Ramakrishna here in 1881.

Lord Vishnu placed his holy foot on demon Gayasura who offered his body for cosmic sacrifice. World-famous for the Pitru Paksha Shraddha pilgrimage where millions offer Pinda Daan for the salvation of ancestors.
temples.Why_Famous: Footprint of Lord Vishnu (40 cm) stamped into solid rock, Pitru Paksha Pinda Daan pilgrimage, 30-metre octagonal grey granite Shikhara built by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar in 1787, holy Falgu River.
temples.Religious_Significance: Mentioned in the Ramayana where Lord Rama and Sita performed Pinda Daan for King Dasharatha; offering Pinda Daan here guarantees liberation for seven generations of ancestors.
temples.Historical_Significance: Reconstructed in 1787 CE by the legendary queen Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore using master stone carvers and grey granite imported from Patharkatti.

temples.Temple_Description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas and also recognized as a Shakti Peeth (where the heart of Sati fell). Enclosed in a fortified courtyard containing 22 temples. Epicentre of the historic 108-km barefoot Shravani Mela Kanwar Yatra from Sultanganj.
temples.Why_Famous: 9th Jyotirlinga, Shravani Mela (world's longest religious walk 108 km from Sultanganj to Deoghar), Punchshool (five-pronged trident) atop the spire, Gathbandhan sacred cloth connecting Shiva and Parvati domes.
temples.Religious_Significance: Demon king Ravana performed severe penance cutting his ten heads to please Shiva; Shiva restored his heads like a physician (Vaidya), hence named Baidyanath.
temples.Historical_Significance: Ancient origin; renovated in 1596 CE by Raja Puran Mal, ancestor of the Maharaja of Gidhaur; British East India Company records document administration from 1788 CE.
temples.Architectural_Style: Nagara (Pyramidal 72-foot stone spire with Panchashoola pinnacle)

temples.Address: Kamakhya, Guwahati, Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam
temples.Main_Deity: Goddess Kamakhya (Natural spring-fed cleft in the subterranean bedrock representing the Yoni of Sati)

temples.Temple_Description: Perched atop the sacred Nilachal Hill overlooking the mighty Brahmaputra River. The supreme seat of Tantric Shaktism and the foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas. The dark subterranean sanctum contains no sculpted idol; worship is offered to a natural fissure in the bedrock fed by an underground natural perennial spring. Features the unique Nilachal hybrid architectural style with a 16-sided beehive dome.
temples.Why_Famous: Foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas, Ambubachi Mela (annual fertility celebration of Mother Earth), natural spring-fed Yoni stone, 10 Mahavidya shrines on Nilachal Hill, Guwahati Passenger Ropeway across Brahmaputra.
temples.Religious_Significance: Goddess Sati's creative womb and yoni fell here during Shiva's Rudra Tandava; celebrated in the Kalika Purana and Yogini Tantra.
temples.Historical_Significance: Stone basements date to 8th-10th century Mlechha and Pala dynasties; destroyed during invasions and rebuilt in stone-and-brick by Koch King Nara Narayana and General Chilarai in 1565 CE.
temples.Architectural_Style: Nilachal Style (Cruciform Base with 16-sided Beehive Bulbous Shikhara)

festivals.Festival_Name: Srivari Annual Salakatla Brahmotsavam, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathasapthami, Ugadi Asthanam
festivals.Description: Garuda Vahanam witnesses over 500,000 devotees circumambulating the Four Mada Streets.

festivals.Festival_Name: Karthika Brahmotsavam, Panchami Theertham, Vasantotsavam, Navaratri
festivals.Description: Lakhs take holy dip in Padma Sarovaram as the divine Chakra Theertham is bathed.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (13 days), Giri Pradakshina, Nandi Seva
festivals.Description: Over 300,000 pilgrims participate in the Rathotsavam and midnight Lingodbhava Abhishekam.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri Brahmotsavam (7 days), Ugadi Mahotsavam, Kumbhothsavam
festivals.Description: Paganalankarana (royal silk turban wrapping around the Vimana) witnessed by over 400,000 pilgrims.
festivals.Source: Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy Devasthanam Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Dasara Navaratri (10 days), Shakambhari Utsavams, Bhavani Deeksha Viramana
festivals.Description: Over 1.5 million devotees gather during Dasara; grand Hamsa Vahana Teppotsavam on Krishna river.
festivals.Source: Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam

festivals.Festival_Name: Annual Brahmotsavam (11 days), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Rathotsavam
festivals.Description: Tirukkalyanam and Divya Vimana Rathotsavam attended by over 300,000 devotees.
festivals.Source: Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA) Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Sri Rama Navami (Kalyanotsavam), Vaikunta Ekadasi (Teppotsavam on Godavari)
festivals.Description: State festival attended by over 400,000 devotees; pearls sent on behalf of state governor.
festivals.Source: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (3-day fair), Ramappa Dance Festival (Kakatiya Heritage Festival)
festivals.Description: Classical dancers from across the world perform before the historic Madanika brackets.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chithirai Thiruvizha (1 month festival), Meenakshi Tirukkalyanam, Navaratri, Avani Moola Utsavam
festivals.Description: Over 1 million devotees witness the Celestial Wedding and Lord Kallazhagar entering Vaigai River.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (10 days), Thirukalyanam (Aadi Amavasai), Ramalinga Prathishta Utsavam
festivals.Description: Hundreds of thousands gather at Agni Theertham for ancestral rites and temple darshan.

festivals.Festival_Name: Sathaya Vizha (Birth anniversary of Raja Raja Chola I), Maha Shivaratri, Chithirai Brahmotsavam
festivals.Description: Grand state celebration featuring classical Bharatanatyam concerts with 1,000 dancers on the temple courtyard.

festivals.Festival_Name: Biennial Paryaya Mahotsava (every 2 years in January), Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Vittal Pindi, Laksha Deepotsava
festivals.Description: Ceremonial transfer of Akshaya Patra and administration to incoming pontiff; Car Street decorated with 100,000 oil lamps during Deepotsava.
festivals.Source: Sri Krishna Matha Paryaya Official Records

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (grand seaside mela and Rathotsava), Karthika Deepotsava
festivals.Description: Massive chariot procession along the beach and night-long coastal bhajan sessions.

festivals.Festival_Name: Alpasi Utsavam, Painkuni Utsavam, Aaraattu (procession to Shangumugham Beach), Lakshadeepam
festivals.Description: Maharaja of Travancore leads the royal procession on foot with drawn sword to Shangumugham Beach.
festivals.Source: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple Official Administrative Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Guruvayur Utsavam (10 days with Elephant Race / Anayottam), Chembai Music Festival, Guruvayur Ekadasi
festivals.Description: Anayottam (legendary elephant race) marks the start of the annual 10-day festival.
festivals.Source: Guruvayur Devaswom Managing Committee Official Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Vinayaka Chaturthi (24-day festival), Brahmotsavam, Sankatahara Chaturthi
festivals.Description: Massive procession of the Golden Chariot through the French and Tamil quarters of Puducherry.
festivals.Source: Government of Puducherry Hindu Religious Institutions Registry

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (continuous 36-hour darshan), Dev Deepawali, Rangbhari Ekadashi, Shravan Maas
festivals.Description: All 84 ghats illuminated with over 1.5 million earthen lamps; lakhs throng the corridor.
festivals.Source: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Sri Rama Navami, Ayodhya Deepotsav (Diwali - Guinness record 2.2 million diyas on Sarayu), Vivaha Panchami
festivals.Description: Surya Tilak: Sunlight is optically focused precisely upon the forehead of Ram Lalla at 12:00 noon on Rama Navami.
festivals.Source: Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Portal

festivals.Festival_Name: Krishna Janmashtami (Midnight Mahapuja), Braj Ki Lathmar Holi, Radhashtami, Sharad Purnima
festivals.Description: Over 1.2 million devotees gather as the Lord is bathed in pure milk, curd, honey, and ghee at the stroke of midnight.
festivals.Source: Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan Directory

festivals.Festival_Name: Kapat Opening (Akshaya Tritiya / May), Kapat Closing (Bhai Dooj / November), Badri-Kedar Utsav
festivals.Month: May to November (Temple closed during winters; deity shifts to Omkareshwar Temple Ukhimath)
festivals.Date: Akshaya Tritiya to Kartik Bhai Dooj
festivals.Description: Ceremonial procession of the Doli carrying the Utsava Murti to Ukhimath for 6 months of winter worship.
festivals.Source: Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Kapat Opening (April/May on Akshaya Tritiya), Badri-Kedar Utsav (June), Kapat Closing (November on Diwali)
festivals.Month: May to November (Closed during winter; deity moves to Narsingh Temple Joshimath)
festivals.Description: The Akhand Jyoti lamp lit inside the sanctum continues burning miraculously throughout the 6 months of winter closure.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navratri & Ashwin Navratri (Lakhs of pilgrims climb to the shrine), Sawan Mela
festivals.Description: Massive fairs with non-stop community kitchens (Langar) across the town.

festivals.Festival_Name: Baisakhi (Khalsa Sirjana Diwas), Prakash Purab Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Bandi Chhor Divas (Diwali Deepmala)
festivals.Description: Spectacular illumination of the Sarovar with hundreds of thousands of earthen lamps and green eco-fireworks.

festivals.Festival_Name: International Gita Mahotsav (December), Surya Grahan Mela, Somvati Amavasya
festivals.Month: November / December (Margashirsha Shukla Ekadasi - Gita Jayanti)
festivals.Description: Over 2 million visitors assemble for Gita recitation and spectacular floating lamps (Deepdan) across the water.

festivals.Festival_Name: Diwali & Annakut (over 1,000 vegetarian food offerings displayed), Janmashtami, Swaminarayan Jayanti
festivals.Description: Colossal illumination of the entire 100-acre campus with lakhs of lamps and spectacular water choreography.

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navratri & Sharad Navratri (Massive decoration with exotic flowers and dry fruits)
festivals.Description: Over 400,000 pilgrims trek during the 9-day festival; telecast live across global networks.
festivals.Source: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ramnavami Utsav (3 days), Guru Purnima Utsav, Vijayadashami (Sai Punyatithi Festival)
festivals.Date: Chaitra Shukla Navami, Ashadha Purnima, Ashwina Dashami
festivals.Description: Continuous 24-hour temple opening; over 300,000 pilgrims participate in Palki processions from Mumbai and Pune.
festivals.Source: Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust Act (Govt of Maharashtra Gazette)

festivals.Festival_Name: Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela (every 12 years), Maha Shivaratri, Tripurari Purnima, Rathotsava
festivals.Month: February / March (Shivaratri) & Kumbh year (Jupiter in Leo)
festivals.Description: Millions of sadhus from Akhadas take holy royal bath (Shahi Snan) at Kushavarta Kund during Kumbh.
festivals.Source: Shri Trimbakeshwar Devasthan Trust Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ganesh Chaturthi (10 days), Angaraki Sankashti Chaturthi, Maghi Ganesh Jayanti
festivals.Date: Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi to Anant Chaturdashi
festivals.Description: Over 200,000 devotees visit every Tuesday; over 1 million during the 10-day Ganeshotsav.
festivals.Source: Shree Siddhi Vinayak Ganpati Temple Trust Act, 1980

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (5-day grand festival), Kartik Purnima Somnath Fair, Shravan Maas
festivals.Description: Continuous 42-hour temple opening on Shivaratri; over 500,000 pilgrims attend the coastal fair.
festivals.Source: Shree Somnath Trust Act & Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Janmashtami Mahotsav, Holi (Dolyatra), Sharad Purnima, Annakut Utsav
festivals.Description: Midnight Kanha Janmotsav attended by over 500,000 devotees dancing with Garba and bhajans.

festivals.Festival_Name: Pushkar Camel Fair & Kartik Purnima Maha Mela (International festival)
festivals.Date: Kartik Shukla Ekadasi to Kartik Purnima
festivals.Description: Attracts over 400,000 tourists and pilgrims worldwide; mass holy dip in Pushkar Lake.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri (9-day Navratri of Shiva ending with Sehra Bandhan), Ujjain Simhastha Kumbh Mela (every 12 years), Shravan Sawari
festivals.Description: Sehra Bandhan on Shivaratri morning; the deity wears a massive floral crown and Bhasma Aarti takes place at noon instead of dawn.
festivals.Source: Shree Mahakaleshwar Temple Management Committee Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Bastar Dussehra (75-day festival), Chaitra & Shardiya Navratri, Fagun Mela (10 days)
festivals.Description: Scores of tribal village shamans assemble carrying local deities on wooden litters to pay homage to Maa Danteshwari.

festivals.Festival_Name: Magha Purnima Jatrotsav (grand annual car festival), Maha Shivaratri, Navaratri
festivals.Description: The deity is taken out in a monumental silver Ratha (chariot) pulled by thousands of devotees.

festivals.Festival_Name: Shree Gundicha Ratha Yatra (Car Festival - 9 days), Snana Yatra, Chandan Yatra (42 days), Bahuda Yatra, Suna Besha
festivals.Description: The Holy Trinity travels 3 km down Bada Danda on massive wooden chariots Nandighosha, Taladhwaja, and Darpadalana; over 1.5 million assemble.
festivals.Source: Shree Jagannatha Temple Act, 1955 (Odisha Act 11 of 1955)

festivals.Festival_Name: Konark Dance Festival (December 1-5 annually against the illuminated temple backdrop), Magha Saptami Chandrabhaga Mela
festivals.Description: World-class classical Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Kuchipudi troupes perform on the open-air stage.

festivals.Festival_Name: Shyama Puja (Deepawali Kali Puja), Kalpataru Utsav (Jan 1), Snana Yatra, Annakut
festivals.Description: Over 500,000 devotees walk across the skywalk on Kalpataru Day when Ramakrishna fulfilled every prayer.
festivals.Source: Dakshineswar Kali Temple Debottar Estate Official Records

festivals.Festival_Name: Pitru Paksha Mela (16 days in Bhadrapada/Ashwina), Chhath Puja, Rama Navami
festivals.Date: Bhadrapada Purnima to Sarva Pitru Amavasya
festivals.Description: Over 2 million pilgrims visit Gaya from across India and the diaspora to offer Pinda Daan rituals at Brahma Kund, Falgu Ghat, and Vishnupad.
festivals.Source: Bihar State Religious Trust Board Register

festivals.Festival_Name: Shravani Mela (month-long monsoon Kanwar festival), Maha Shivaratri, Basant Panchami
festivals.Date: Full month of Shravan (Ashadha Purnima to Shravana Purnima)
festivals.Description: Over 6 million saffron-clad pilgrims (Kanwariyas) walk 108 km barefoot carrying Ganga water from Sultanganj in pots balanced on bamboo poles.
festivals.Source: Baba Baidyanath Dham Temple Management Act & Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Ambubachi Mela (Monsoon in June - 4 days), Durga Puja (Navaratri with buffalo sacrifice traditions), Manasa Puja
festivals.Description: Sanctum doors remain shut for 3 full days commemorating the annual menstrual cycle of the Earth Goddess; reopened on 4th day with distribution of sacred red cloth (Angodak/Raktavastra).
festivals.Source: Maa Kamakhya Devalaya Bordeuri Samaj Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Diwali Matabari Mela (2-day state festival with lakhs of pilgrims), Navaratri
festivals.Description: Over 300,000 pilgrims congregate around Kalyan Sagar lake to light lamps and seek blessings.
festivals.Source: Maa Tripura Sundari Temple Trust Official Gazette

festivals.Festival_Name: Panguni Uthiram (Grand Chariot Festival), Thaipusam (Kavadi procession), Skanda Sashti
festivals.Description: Lakhs of island residents participate in the pulling of the golden chariot through the streets of Port Blair.
festivals.Source: Directorate of Tourism, Andaman & Nicobar Administration Directory

festivals.Festival_Name: Chaitra Navaratri; Sharad Navaratri; Maha Shivaratri
festivals.Description: Grand nine-day celebration with massive regional gatherings.

festivals.Festival_Name: Maha Shivaratri; Shravan Maas Somwar; Kartik Purnima
festivals.State: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
festivals.Description: All-night vigil and coastal prayers during Maha Shivaratri.
festivals.Source: Daman and Diu Tourism Department & District Administration

festivals.Festival_Name: Krishna Janmashtami; Diwali; Holi; Ram Navami
festivals.Description: Grand Janmashtami celebration with community feast and cultural programs.

festivals.Festival_Name: Kali Puja; Durga Puja; Saraswati Puja; Shivaratri
festivals.Description: Largest Hindu gathering in Mizoram during Diwali and Durga Puja.
Celebrated with island-wide interfaith harmony and coastal defense prayers.
